question: Will November 2026 be the warmest November on record, according to Copernicus?

calls.reasoning: November record is Nov 2023 at +0.85C (ERA5, vs 1991-2020). Oct 2026 is tracking as the warmest October on record (~+0.92C per celsius.earth/ERA5) with late-October dailies ~+1.10C (record for the date). A record-strength, still-strengthening El Nino (Nino3.4 weekly +3.3C mid-Oct; all models very strong through DJF), plus the usual lag of global temperatures, pushes November upward. November needs only to avoid a drop of more than ~0.07C from October's anomaly; typical month-to-month changes are ~0.1C. Counter: celsius.earth's own November model gives 42% (mean +0.83C), and October figures are third-party and not yet official. No market found.

calls.reconciliation: The key factual dispute was whether October 2026 is at +0.92C or +0.84C. The live celsius.earth/warmest-month page (generated 2026-10-30 08:43 UTC, 29/31 days) shows +0.92C, 0.07C above Oct 2023; the +0.84C and +0.23C snippets conflict with live pages and are most likely stale. The front page confirms the 29 Oct daily at +1.10C vs 1991-2020, so the baseline is no longer unclear. The tracker's Nov model (+0.83, 42%) seems to have under-forecast October by about 0.08C, so I weight it modestly. The judgment calls (2023 levelling off, noise) favour persistence. Final 0.79 sits between Run 1 and Runs 2/3 because the factual check upheld October's record-level warmth while the tracker's model remains a real counterweight.
